critical_code_review_comments: Fix is minimal and correct: registering the already-defined async startup_stripe() via app.add_event_handler('startup', startup_stripe) at server.py:5716. On boot, _ensure_stripe_prices() successfully populated STRIPE_PRICE_IDS (verified because /api/billing/plans now returns non-null stripe_price_id and checkout returns cs_live_ URLs).

Minor terminology mismatch between review request and code: the review says data-testid='topup-<id>' for the clickable purchase button, but in Billing.jsx L449 topup-<id> is the outer card wrapper and L459 defines the actual button as data-testid='buy-<id>'. Consider unifying by renaming the button to 'topup-<id>' (or the wrapper), which would remove ambiguity in future test writing. Non-blocking.

Consider adding an explicit log line in startup_stripe() (already exists per main-agent note 'Stripe price provisioning complete') plus a boot-time assert or fallback so a Stripe API outage during startup does not silently leave STRIPE_PRICE_IDS empty. If _ensure_stripe_prices() raises, currently the FastAPI startup would fail (which is acceptable, but ensure the log is loud). Non-blocking.

rca of the issue: RCA: startup_stripe() was defined at server.py:2940 (async, calls _ensure_stripe_prices() to look up or create Stripe products+prices and populate the in-memory STRIPE_PRICE_IDS dict) but was NEVER registered as a FastAPI startup event. Because STRIPE_PRICE_IDS stayed empty at runtime, POST /api/billing/checkout/subscription hit the guard at L3085 (and topup at L3132) and raised HTTPException(503, 'Plan price not provisioned yet'). REPRO: rollback L5716 → sign up trial vendor → click Upgrade Basic → toast 'Plan price not provisioned yet' (was reproduced pre-fix by main agent). MITIGATION: added app.add_event_handler('startup', startup_stripe) at server.py:5716 alongside _email_start and _sales_start. Verified post-fix: /api/billing/plans returns populated stripe_price_ids, checkout endpoints return cs_live_ URLs. No further action needed.
